To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mutant protein UBB+1 accumulates in Alzheimer's disease and is not degraded by cellular proteases.
UBB+1, a mutant form of ubiquitin that is found in neurones of patients suffering from AD, has lost its capacity to ubiquitinate, but is still able to be ubiquitinated.

1) UBB+1 does not ubiquitinate and is ubiquitinated; 2) UBB+ 1 is quite stable in cells; 3) overexpression of UBB +1 in neuronal cells induces nuclear fragmentation and neuronal death; 4) UBB+ is a toxic mutant ubiquitin that may be involved in the neurotoxicity of AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and its role in Alzheimer's disease.
the role of mutant ubiquitin (UBB+) in neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease.
the role of ubiquitin and ubiquitin‐related molecules in neurodegenerative disorders.
